sections.html:
Alexandria is a central Louisiana city beside the Red River, and Rapides Parish government is based here. The 2020 count was 45,275 people, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 42,938. The wider metro area has 153,922 people, so the pool of possible buyers reaches well beyond the city limits.

Pineville faces Alexandria from the far bank, linked by three road bridges: the Purple Heart Memorial Bridge, the U.S. 165 Business (Gillis Long) Bridge and the Curtis-Coleman (Fort Buhlow) Bridge. Many buyers work on the opposite bank, so expect questions about commute times during showings. Interstate 49 runs through town, and Louisiana Highway 1 connects Alexandria to Baton Rouge.

Per capita income was $23,962 in 2016, which is $1,702 below the state average. Price-sensitive buyers are common, so a house that needs work gets measured against move-in ready listings.

Most seller paperwork in Alexandria runs through three Rapides Parish offices plus a few state bodies.

TaskWhere it goes
Property value and homestead statusRapides Parish assessor
Tax bill and paymentRapides Parish tax collector
Recording the deedRapides Parish Clerk of Court
Disputing an assessed valueLocal Board of Review, then the Louisiana Tax Commission

Phone the assessor about exemption questions and the clerk for a copy of your last deed.

sections.h2: Property taxes on an Alexandria house
sections.html:
Your tax bill comes from parish offices, not city hall. The Rapides Parish assessor puts a value on the house, and the parish tax collector mails the invoice. Homes are taxed on 10 percent of fair market value. Invoices arrive in December and are due by December 31. After that, 1 percent interest is added for every month the balance sits unpaid.

The assessor lets owners look over the roll from August 15 to September 15 each year (Orleans Parish runs on a different schedule). Use it to check how your own house was valued. If the number looks too high, start with the local Board of Review. A Board ruling you still dispute can go on to the Louisiana Tax Commission.

Before you pick a closing date, get the exact balance from the Rapides Parish tax collector.

A home you live in can carry a homestead exemption worth $7,500 of assessed value. A buyer who does not live there, or who has not yet filed, may see a different bill than you did. Ask the assessor whether your exemption is on file before you list, because a gap is simpler to fix ahead of the title search than in the middle of it.

Back taxes do not block a sale. They get paid out of what you receive at closing. La. R.S. 47:1993 turns the assessor's roll, once it reaches the recorder of mortgages, into a lien and privilege on every assessed property, and that lien usually outranks other claims. Until those taxes are cleared the title company cannot give the buyer a clean policy, so the payoff simply becomes a line on your settlement sheet.

When more than one year is unpaid, request a written payoff from the tax collector and hand it to your closing attorney or notary. Get it before you accept an offer so your net figure is real.

sections.h2: How a sale closes in Alexandria
sections.html:
Alexandria sales are handled by an attorney or notary, who runs a title search and prepares the act of sale. The finished deed is filed at the Rapides Parish Clerk of Court. The usual order of events:

  1. Sign a purchase agreement with the buyer.
  2. The attorney or notary orders a title search and checks for liens, including property taxes.
  3. Your lender supplies a mortgage payoff figure.
  4. Seller and buyer sign the act of sale in front of the notary.
  5. The clerk records the act, and taxes and loan balances come out of your proceeds.

Having your deed, survey and latest tax bill ready, plus repair, insurance and flood records, speeds up every step.

Closing costs and payoffs are settled at the table, so ask for a draft settlement statement a few days ahead and read each line. Questions about a fee or a lien are much easier to resolve before signing day than after the act is recorded.

Rain is the main hazard for Alexandria houses: the city is humid subtropical, with 60.90 inches in an average year, hot summers and mild winters. Hurricane Gustav in 2008 caused widespread flooding in the city, and some low-lying neighborhoods had several feet of water inside houses. Snow is rare, though the average first freeze arrives in early to mid November, so pipes in unheated houses can be exposed on a few nights each year.

Own a house in a low area? Pull together flood insurance records, repair invoices and any elevation certificate before listing. Buyers and lenders will ask about water history, and a folder of paper answers faster than a long conversation.

sections.h2: What to bring and how long it takes
sections.html:
Paperwork on hand can shave days off a sale. Before meeting an attorney, notary or buyer, collect the deed you received, the survey, the newest tax bill, your lender's contact details and any repair or flood records. An inherited house also needs proof of who is allowed to sign.

A financed sale waits on the buyer's loan, an appraisal and an inspection. With cash there are fewer moving parts, and the date mostly depends on the title search and on when you and the notary can meet. Either way, every few days ask the attorney or notary what is still outstanding.

With no lender involved, there is no loan approval to wait for. Many cash buyers take the house as-is, so the leaky roof, old wiring or damp room stays their problem. You also skip repeated open houses and the chance that a financed buyer walks away after inspection.

You give up some price. Cash offers tend to land below a fully repaired listing, so compare the number against repair bills, carrying costs and time. Taxes and any mortgage still come out of the proceeds either way.

sections.h2: Ways to sell and what each asks of you
sections.html:
There are three common routes in Alexandria: an agent listing, a sale on your own, or a cash offer. Pick based on the house's condition, your deadline and how many showings you can stand.

  • Listing: Widest exposure, but financing, appraisal and inspection all have to clear.
  • Selling on your own: No agent commission, but screening buyers and paperwork are on you.
  • Cash offer: Quick and usually as-is, so repairs and showings may not be needed.

Local sellers often deal with storm or water damage, aging systems, inheritance or a short timeline. Set any as-is offer beside the cost to repair and list, and beside your net after taxes and liens.

faqs.q: How many people live in Alexandria, Louisiana?
faqs.a: The city had 45,275 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 42,938 as of July 1, 2025. Across the whole metro area the count is 153,922.
Rapides Parish. Alexandria is its parish seat, and Pineville lies across the Red River.

faqs.q: When are Alexandria property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 31, with bills mailed that December and 1 percent monthly interest on late balances. The Rapides Parish tax collector can confirm this year's details.
Yes. Hurricane Gustav in 2008 flooded much of the city, and low-lying neighborhoods saw several feet of water indoors. Keep repair and insurance records handy.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Alexandria house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The taxes are settled from your proceeds at closing, because under La. R.S. 47:1993 they are a lien the title company must account for.
